'''Titan Company Limited''' is an Indian [[Fashion accessory|fashion accessories]] company that mainly manufactures items such as [[jewellery]], [[watches]] and [[eyewear]]. Part of the [[Tata Group]] and started as a joint venture with [[Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation|TIDCO]], the company has its corporate headquarters in [[Electronic City]], [[Bangalore]],<ref>{{cite news|title=When an office becomes a people's home|work=Livemint|url=https://www.livemint.com/Leisure/9I4MxLkSQeK9myy0YsBxhM/When-an-office-becomes-a-peoples-home.html|access-date=17 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108111655/https://www.livemint.com/Leisure/9I4MxLkSQeK9myy0YsBxhM/When-an-office-becomes-a-peoples-home.html|archive-date=8 November 2020}}</ref> and registered office in [[Hosur]], [[Tamil Nadu]].<ref>{{cite news|title=A Titan of Bengaluru|language=en|work=The Times of India|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/a-titan-of-bengaluru/articleshow/59641915.cms|access-date=7 December 2021|archive-date=7 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211207191948/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/a-titan-of-bengaluru/articleshow/59641915.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

Titan Company commenced operations in 1984 under the name Titan Watches Limited. In 1994, Titan diversified into jewellery with [[Tanishq]] and subsequently into eyewear with Titan Eyeplus. In 2005, it launched its youth fashion accessories brand [[Fastrack (fashion accessories)|Fastrack]].<ref>{{cite news|date=27 May 2008|title=On the Fastrack|work=The Financial ==History==
===1984–1990===
Titan Company Limited was inaugurated on 26 July 1984 under the name Titan Watches Limited in [[Chennai]].<ref name="titan-history">{{Cite news|url=https://www.goodreturns.in/company/titan/history.html|title=Titan Company Ltd. Company History and Annual Growth Details|publisher=goodreturns.in|access-date=7 October 2018|archive-date=7 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181007223246/https://www.goodreturns.in/company/titan/history.html|url-status=live}}</ref> A plant was set up to manufacture quartz analogue electronic watches in the [[State Industries Promotion Corporation of Tamil Nadu]] industrial area at [[Hosur]]. In November 1986, Titan Company and [[Casio]] signed a [[Memorandum of understanding|MoU]] to manufacture 2 million digital and analog-digital watches.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/titan-company-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-12903.cms|title=Titan Company Ltd.|publisher=Economic Times|access-date=7 October 2018|archive-date=6 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706111814/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/titan-company-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-12903.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

===1991–2010===
In 1992, [[Timex Group USA|Timex]] entered the Indian market by establishing a joint venture with Titan Watches. Under the agreement, Timex manufactured lower-priced watches, which were marketed and sold in Titan stores alongside Titan's higher-end watches.<ref name="timex">{{cite news |title=Titan, Timex Wind Up Marketing Alliance |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/specials/titan-timex-wind-up-marketing-alliance-197122301097_1.html |access-date=6 April 2025 |work=Business Standard |date=23 December 1997}}</ref>

In September 1993, Titan Watches changed its name to Titan Industries as it ventured into products other than watches.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/titan-eyes-1520-growth-in-jewellery/article8576680.ece|title=Titan eyes growth in jewellery|date=9 May 2016|access-date=26 December 2016|archive-date=19 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019021257/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/titan-eyes-1520-growth-in-jewellery/article8576680.ece|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/titan-company-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-12903.cms|title=Titan Company Ltd.|publisher=Economic Times|access-date=14 October 2018|archive-date=7 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181007224553/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/titan-company-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-12903.cms|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1994, Titan launched its jewellery brand [[Tanishq]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bestmediainfo.com/2017/06/titan-consolidates-its-ooh-biz-with-milestone-brandcom-and-laqshya-media/|title=Titan consolidates its OOH biz with Milestone Brandcom and Laqshya Media|publisher=Best Media Info|date=14 June 2017|access-date=14 October 2018|archive-date=6 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706111850/https://www.bestmediainfo.com/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 1997, Titan and Timex terminated their partnership.<ref name="timex"/> In a bid to compete with Timex, Titan soon after launched a range of economy watches under Sonata,<ref>{{cite news |title=The Long And The Short |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/specials/the-long-and-the-short-198011201073_1.html |access-date=6 April 2025 |work=Business Standard |date=12 January 1998}}</ref> and a watch and accessories sub-brand, Fastrack, which was targeted at younger customers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2005/dec/01titan.htm|title=Titan's Fastrack on comeback trail|work=rediff.com|date=1 December 2005|access-date=14 October 2018|archive-date=11 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011170300/http://www.rediff.com/money/2005/dec/01titan.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2004, Titan signed an agreement with the [[Mohan Murjani|Murjani Group]] to market and distribute the latter's [[Tommy Hilfiger (company)|Tommy Hilfiger]] watches in India.<ref>{{cite news |title=Titan, Murjanis to sell Tommy Hilfiger watches |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/titan-murjanis-to-sell-tommy-hilfiger-watches-104030201076_1.html |access-date=6 April 2025 |work=Business Standard |date=2 March 2004}}</ref> 2004, Titan partnered with [[LVMH]] to service the latter's watches in India through its service centres.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2004/11/25/stories/2004112502150400.htm|title=The Hindu Business Line : Titan in service pact with LVMH Group|website=www.thehindubusinessline.com|access-date=3 November 2018|archive-date=14 February 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090214092730/http://thehindubusinessline.com/2004/11/25/stories/2004112502150400.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2005, [[Fastrack (fashion accessories)|Fastrack]] was positioned as an independent accessory brand targeting the urban youth. To become a fashion brand, Fastrack launched [[sunglasses]] in the same year and launched bags, belts and wallets in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afaqs.com/news/story/42819_Fastrack-Bold-Statements|title=Fastrack: Bold Statements|website=www.afaqs.com|date=22 December 2014 |language=en|access-date=3 November 2018|archive-date=3 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103131302/https://www.afaqs.com/news/story/42819_Fastrack-Bold-Statements|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2007, Titan established its [[Eyeglass prescription|prescription eyewear]] store chain called Titan Eyeplus.<ref>{{cite news |title=Titan enters eyewear market |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/titan-enters-eyewear-market-107033001063_1.html |access-date=6 April 2025 |work=Business Standard |date=30 March 2007}}</ref> Titan launched a multi-brand luxury watch store format called Helios in 2009.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sachitanand |first=Rahul |title=Titan springs back |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/features/story/titan-springs-back-17102-2010-05-26 |access-date=6 April 2025 |work=Business Today |date=26 May 2010 |language=en}}</ref>

===2011–present===
[[File:Tanishq jewellers, chaitanyapuri, Dilsukhnagar, Hyderabad.jpg|thumb|A Tanishq jewellery store in Hyderabad.]]
Titan acquired Swiss watchmaker [[Favre-Leuba]] in 2011 for €2 million to enter the [[European single market|European market]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.livemint.com/Industry/GMGi4WqkMyrhOfdz05zmRL/Titan-ties-up-with-Ethos-Watches-to-relaunch-FavreLeuba-wat.html|title=Favre-Leuba 3.0: cashing in emotionally|date=6 December news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/titan-launches-skinn-fragrance-line-113091600764_1.html|title=Titan launches 'Skinn' fragrance line|last=Badrinath|first=Raghuvir|date=16 helmets category under the Fastrack brand.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/titan-launches-helmets-under-fastrack-brand/article5418721.ece|title=Titan launches helmets under Fastrack brand|work=The Hindu|access-date=9 March 2017|language=en|archive-date=17 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131217091201/http://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/titan-launches-helmets-under-fastrack-brand/article5418721.ece|url-status=live}}</ref> In the same year, it changed its name to Titan Company Ltd.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/titan-company-1016/information/company-history|title=Titan Company Ltd.|work=Business 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103092103/https://www.business-standard.com/company/titan-company-1016/information/company-history|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2014, it entered into a joint venture with [[Montblanc (company)|Montblanc]] to establish its retail stores in India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/announcements/titan-company-enters-into-jvmontblanc-services-bv-netherlands-1114685.html|title=Titan Company enters into JV with Montblanc Services BV, Netherlands|website=Money Control|date=27 February 2014 |language=en-US|access-date=3 November 2018|archive-date=3 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103092136/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/announcements/titan-company-enters-into-jvmontblanc-services-bv-netherlands-1114685.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2016, Titan entered the wearable devices market by introducing its [[smartwatch]], Juxt, made through a collaboration with [[Hewlett-Packard]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/electronics/titan-launches-smartwatch-juxt-with-hp-inc/articleshow/50658613.cms|title=Titan launches smartwatch JUXT with HP Inc|date=20 January 2016|work=The Economic Times|access-date=3 July 2019|archive-date=3 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703155102/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/electronics/titan-launches-smartwatch-juxt-with-hp-inc/articleshow/50658613.cms|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2017, the company launched a [[Activity tracker|fitness tracker]], named Gesture Band under its youth accessories brand, Fastrack.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/fastrack-eyes-the-no-2-position-in-the-smart-wearables-category-in-india/article25625299.ece|title=Fastrack eyes the No. 2 position in the smart wearables category in India|website=Hindu Business Line|date=29 November 2018 |language=en|access-date=3 July 2019|archive-date=10 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200910194712/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/fastrack-eyes-the-no-2-position-in-the-smart-wearables-category-in-india/article25625299.ece|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2018, the company added new fitness tracker bands. The company had a 7.4% market share in the wearable devices market as of 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/retail/exclusive-titan-to-expand-into-smart-watches-and-fitness-wearables-says-md-bhaskar-bhat6-32961.htm|title=Exclusive: Titan to expand into smart watches and fitness wearables, says MD Bhaskar Bhat|website=cnbctv18.com|date=12 April 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=3 July 2019|archive-date=3 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703155102/https://www.cnbctv18.com/retail/exclusive-titan-to-expand-into-smart-watches-and-fitness-wearables-says-md-bhaskar-bhat6-32961.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2017, Titan started its women's ethnic wear retail chain named Taneira.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Govind |first1=Deepti |title=Titan opens first womens-wear handloom store Taneira in Bengaluru |url=https://www.livemint.com/Industry/rr7N6Pe9CJ8l1wuSv7fI2O/Titan-enters-womenswear-segment-with-first-handloom-store-T.html |access-date=6 April 2025 |work=Mint |date=27 February 2017}}</ref> In 2018, Titan merged its South India-focused jewellery brand Gold Plus with Tanishq.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/titan-to-merge-gold-plus-brand-with-tanishq-117011601132_1.html|title=Titan to merge 'Gold Plus' brand with Tanishq|date=16 January 2017|work=Business Standard India|access-date=3 November 2018|archive-date=3 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103092038/https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/titan-to-merge-gold-plus-brand-with-tanishq-117011601132_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In November 2020, Titan opened its first overseas Tanishq store in [[Dubai]].<ref>{{cite news |last= |first= |date=3 November 2020|title=Titan Company launches first overseas Tanishq store in Dubai|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/titan-company-launches-first-overseas-tanishq-store-in-dubai-11604404723423.html|newspaper=Live Mint}}</ref>

In 2023, Titan sold its subsidiary Favre-Leuba to Ethos.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bench |first=Bar & |date=2023-05-29 |title=Anand and Anand acts for Ethos in its global acquisition of Favre Leuba |url=https://www.barandbench.com/law-firms/dealstreet/anand-and-anand-act-for-ethos-in-its-global-acquisition-of-favre-leuba |access-date=2023-08-20 |website=Bar and Bench - Indian Legal news |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Menon |first1=Murali K |title=Will Favre Leuba soar again? |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/lifestyle/fashion/will-favre-leuba-soar-again-101715589959187.html |access-date=21 June 2024 |work=Hindustan Times |date=13 May 2024}}</ref>

In 2025, the company forayed into the lab-grown diamonds category by launching beYon - from the House of Titan with an exclusive retail store in Mumbai as a part of ongoing strategy to cater to the adornment needs of women in lifestyle categories beyond watches, perfumes, sarees and handbags.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meirovich |first=Leah |date=2025-12-28 |title=No Longer Coy, Titan Moves into Lab-Grown |url=https://rapaport.com/news/no-longer-coy-titan-moves-into-lab-grown/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=Rapaport |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Subsidiaries and affiliate companies==

Titan Engineering & Automation Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary of Titan. It was formerly known as Titan-Precision Engineering Division. The company now deals in machine building, automation and component manufacturing.<ref name="subsidiaries">{{Cite web|url=https://www.titancompany.in/subsidiaries|title=Subsidiaries Titan Corporate|website=www.titancompany.in|access-date=20 February 2019|archive-date=21 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221000230/https://www.titancompany.in/subsidiaries|url-status=live}}</ref>

Titan Company acquired the historic Swiss watch brand Favre-Leuba in November 2011 for US$2.7 million.

In 2015, Titan entered a joint venture to sell products of the Swiss luxury brand [[Montblanc (company)|Montblanc]] through its retail outlets. Titan's equity share in Montblanc India Retail Private Limited is 49% and Montblanc Services B.V. holds 51%.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 December 2015 |title=Titan appoints directors for new JV with Maison Montblanc |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/titan-appoints-directors-for-new-jv-with-maison-montblanc/article7958442.ece |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011012031/https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/titan-appoints-directors-for-new-jv-with-maison-montblanc/article7958442.ece |archive-date=11 October 2021 |access-date=20 February 2019 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN}}</ref>

In 2016, Titan acquired a 62% stake in [[CaratLane]] for {{INRconvert|357|c|mode=historical|year=2016}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/fashion-/-cosmetics-/-jewellery/titan-to-acquire-62-per-cent-stake-in-carat-lane-for-rs-357-24-crore/articleshow/53214980.cms|title=Titan to acquire 62 per cent stake in Carat Lane for Rs 357.24 crore|date=14 July 2016|work=The Economic Times|access-date=20 February 2019|archive-date=21 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221000415/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/fashion-/-cosmetics-/-jewellery/titan-to-acquire-62-per-cent-stake-in-carat-lane-for-rs-357-24-crore/articleshow/53214980.cms|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2023, Titan acquired another 27.18% stake in CaratLane from its founder and his family for {{INRconvert|4621|c|mode=historical|year=2023}} in cash, following which its stake in the company increased to 98.28%.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mukul |first=Pranav |date=2023-08-19 |title=Titan picks up 27% more in CaratLane for Rs 4,621 crore |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/titan-buys-remaining-27-stake-in-caratlane-for-rs-4600-crore/articleshow/102852413.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-08-20 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> In 2024, Titan acquired the remaining stake in CaratLane.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 February 2024 |title=Titan Company to acquire remaining 0.36% stake in CaratLane for Rs 60.08 crore |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-titan-company-to-acquire-remaining-0-36-stake-in-caratlane-for-rs-6008-crore-3407039/ |access-date=4 December 2024 |website=Financial Express}}</ref>

In mid-2025, Titan Company Limited acquired 67% stake in the UAE-based Damas Jewellery and enables the company's expansion across the six GCC countries - UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain.<ref>{{Cite news |last=PTI |date=2025-07-21 |title=Titan to acquire 67% stake in UAE-based Damas jewellery |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/titan-to-acquire-67-stake-in-uae-based-damas-jewellery/article69839943.ece |access-date=2026-03-18 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

extract:
Titan Company Limited is an Indian fashion accessories company that mainly manufactures items such as jewellery, watches and eyewear. Part of the Tata Group and started as a joint venture with TIDCO, the company has its corporate headquarters in Electronic City, Bangalore, and registered office in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.
Titan Company commenced operations in 1984 under the name Titan Watches Limited. In 1994, Titan diversified into jewellery with Tanishq and subsequently into eyewear with Titan Eyeplus. In 2005, it launched its youth fashion accessories brand Fastrack. Titan is the largest branded jewellery maker in India by value, with a 6% market share as of 2022. More than 80% of its total revenue comes from the jewellery segment. As of 2019, it is also the fifth-largest watch manufacturer in the world by volume.
